item.title: Layers in neural network
item.description:
What are layers?

Layers are the fundamental building blocks of neural networks. In PyTorch, layers are modular components that transform input data through learned parameters (weights and biases). Each layer performs a specific mathematical operation, and by stacking multiple layers together, we can create complex neural networks capable of learning intricate patterns.

Common Types of Layers in PyTorch

1. Linear Layers (Fully Connected)

The most basic layer type that connects every input neuron to every output neuron. Each connection has a learnable weight, making it ideal for learning general relationships between features.

item.title: How to build and train a simple Neural Network using pytorch
item.description:
PyTorch

PyTorch is a famous tool to build neural networks which can be used with Python .

Installation

First, install PyTorch using pip:

BASH 
pip install torch torchvision
Click to expand and view more

Building a Simple Neural Network

Step 1: Import Required Libraries

PYTHON 
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
Click to expand and view more

Step 2: Define the Network Architecture

PYTHON 
class SimpleNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_size, hidden_size, output_size):
        super(SimpleNN, self).__init__()
        self.layer1 = nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.layer2 = nn.Linear(hidden_size, output_size)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.layer1(x)
        x = self.relu(x)
        x = self.layer2(x)
        return x

Step 3: Initialize the Model

PYTHON 
# Define dimensions
input_size = 10
hidden_size = 20
output_size = 2

# Create model instance
model = SimpleNN(input_size, hidden_size, output_size)
Click to expand and view more

Step 4: Define Loss Function and Optimizer

PYTHON 
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
Click to expand and view more

Step 5: Training Loop

PYTHON 
# Example training loop
for epoch in range(100):
    # Forward pass
    outputs = model(train_data)
    loss = criterion(outputs, train_labels)
    
    # Backward pass and optimization
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    
    if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
        print(f'Epoch [{epoch+1}/100], Loss: {loss.item():.4f}')
Click to expand and view more

Key Concepts

  • nn.Module: Base class for all neural network modules
  • Forward pass: Defines how data flows through the network
  • Loss function: Measures how well the model performs
  • Optimizer: Updates the model weights to minimize loss
  • Backpropagation: Automatic gradient computation using .backward()

Conclusion

PyTorch makes it easy to build and train neural networks with its intuitive API and automatic differentiation capabilities. This simple example demonstrates the core workflow that can be extended to more complex architectures.
